subject: Chemistry
stem: The ratio of the wavelengths of the light absorbed by a Hydrogen atom when it undergoes \(n = 2 \rightarrow n = 3\) and \(n = 4 \rightarrow n = 6\) transitions, respectively, is
solution: \(\Delta E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} = E_{final} - E_{initial}\), with \(E_n = \dfrac{-R_H}{n^2}\). For \(2\rightarrow 3\): \(\Delta E_{2\rightarrow 3} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{4}-\dfrac{1}{9}\right) = R_H\times\dfrac{5}{36}\), so \(\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3} = \dfrac{hc\cdot 36}{R_H\cdot 5}\). For \(4\rightarrow 6\): \(\Delta E_{4\rightarrow 6} = R_H\left(\dfrac{1}{16}-\dfrac{1}{36}\right) = \dfrac{R_H\times 20}{36\times 16}\), so \(\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6} = \dfrac{hc\times 36\times 16}{R_H\cdot 20}\). Therefore \(\dfrac{\lambda_{2\rightarrow 3}}{\lambda_{4\rightarrow 6}} = \dfrac{1}{4}\).

subject: Chemistry
chapter: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
stem:
Which of the following statements are true?

A. Unlike Ga that has a very high melting point, Cs has a very low melting point.
B. On Pauling scale, the electronegativity values of N and Cl are not the same.
C. Ar, \(\text{K}^{+}\), \(\text{Cl}^{-}\), \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\), and \(\text{S}^{2-}\) are all isoelectronic species.
D. The correct order of the first ionization enthalpies of Na, Mg, Al, and Si is Si > Al > Mg > Na.
E. The atomic radius of Cs is greater than that of Li and Rb.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Both Ga (mp 303 K) and Cs (mp 302 K) have low melting points, so A is false. On the Pauling scale, N and Cl have the same electronegativity (3.0), so B is false. Ar, \(\text{K}^{+}\), \(\text{Cl}^{-}\), \(\text{Ca}^{2+}\) and \(\text{S}^{2-}\) all have 18 electrons, so they are isoelectronic (C true). The correct order of first ionization enthalpy is Si > Mg > Al > Na (Mg higher than Al because 3s-electron penetration is more than 2p), so D is false. Down the group atomic radius increases (Li 152, Rb 244, Cs 262 pm), so E is true. Correct: C and E only.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Predict the major product 'P' in the following sequence of reactions: 1-methylcyclopent-1-ene is treated with (i) HBr, benzoyl peroxide; (ii) KCN; (iii) Na(Hg)/\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\) to give P (Major).
options: 2-methylcyclopentane bearing a \(\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2\) group on the adjacent carbon (1-methyl-2-(aminomethyl)cyclopentane)
solution: HBr with benzoyl peroxide adds anti-Markovnikov, placing Br on the carbon adjacent to the methyl-bearing carbon. KCN performs nucleophilic substitution giving the nitrile (\(\text{-CN}\)) on that adjacent carbon. Na(Hg)/\(\text{C}_2\text{H}_5\text{OH}\) reduces the nitrile to \(\text{-CH}_2\text{NH}_2\). The product P has \(\text{CH}_3\) and \(\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2\) on adjacent ring carbons.

stem:
Which of the following are paramagnetic?

A. \([\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}\)
B. \(\text{Ni(CO)}_4\)
C. \([\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}\)
D. \([\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\)
E. \(\text{Ni(PPh}_3)_4\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: \([\text{NiCl}_4]^{2-}\): \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\), \(3d^8\), \(sp^3\), 2 unpaired electrons, paramagnetic. \(\text{Ni(CO)}_4\): Ni, \(sp^3\), 0 unpaired, diamagnetic. \([\text{Ni(CN)}_4]^{2-}\): \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\), \(dsp^2\), 0 unpaired, diamagnetic. \([\text{Ni(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{2+}\): \(\text{Ni}^{2+}\), \(sp^3d^2\), 2 unpaired, paramagnetic. \(\text{Ni(PPh}_3)_4\): Ni, \(sp^3\), 0 unpaired, diamagnetic. Paramagnetic: A and D only.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Like nitrogen that can form ammonia, arsenic can form arsine.

Statement II: Antimony cannot form antimony pentoxide.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: All group 15 elements form hydrides of \(\text{EH}_3\) type; nitrogen forms ammonia (\(\text{NH}_3\)) and arsenic forms arsine (\(\text{AsH}_3\)), so Statement I is correct. Group 15 elements form two types of oxides \(\text{E}_2\text{O}_3\) and \(\text{E}_2\text{O}_5\); antimony forms antimony pentoxide \(\text{Sb}_2\text{O}_5\), so Statement II is incorrect.

Which among the following electronic configurations belong to main group elements?

A. \([\text{Ne}]3s^1\)
B. \([\text{Ar}]3d^3 4s^2\)
C. \([\text{Kr}]4d^{10}\,5s^2 5p^5\)
D. \([\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^1\)
E. \([\text{Rn}]5f^0 6d^2 7s^2\)

Choose the correct answer from the option given below:
solution: A: \([\text{Ne}]3s^1\) = Na (s-block, main group). B: \([\text{Ar}]3d^3 4s^2\) = V (d-block). C: \([\text{Kr}]4d^{10}5s^2 5p^5\) = I (p-block, main group). D: \([\text{Ar}]3d^{10}4s^1\) = Cu (d-block). E: \([\text{Rn}]5f^0 6d^2 7s^2\) = Th (f-block). Main group elements: A and C only.

solution: Dalton's theory could explain the laws of chemical combination. However, it could not explain the law of gaseous volumes.

stem: Consider the following compounds: \(\underline{\text{K}}\text{O}_2\), \(\text{H}_2\underline{\text{O}}_2\) and \(\text{H}_2\underline{\text{S}}\text{O}_4\). The oxidation state of the underlined elements in them are, respectively,
solution: In \(\text{KO}_2\), the alkali metal K always shows +1. In \(\text{H}_2\text{O}_2\), oxygen has oxidation state \(-1\) (peroxide linkage). In \(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4\), sulphur has oxidation state +6. Hence +1, \(-1\), and +6.

subject: Chemistry
stem: If the half-life (\(t_{1/2}\)) for a first order reaction is 1 minute, then the time required for 99.9% completion of the reaction is closest to:
solution: For a first order reaction, \(kt = 2.303\log\dfrac{A_0}{A_t}\). The time for 99.9% completion equals \(10\,t_{1/2}\). So \(t_{99.9\%} = 10 \times 1\text{ minute} = 10\text{ minutes}\).

stem:
The correct order of the wavelength of light absorbed by the following complexes is,

A. \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\)
B. \([\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{3-}\)
C. \([\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O})_4]^{2+}\)
D. \([\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: \(\lambda \propto \dfrac{1}{\text{strength of ligand}} \propto \dfrac{1}{\text{splitting}}\). Absorption wavelengths: A \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+}\) 475 nm; B \([\text{Co(CN)}_6]^{3-}\) 310 nm; C \([\text{Cu(H}_2\text{O})_4]^{2+}\) 600 nm; D \([\text{Ti(H}_2\text{O})_6]^{3+}\) 498 nm. Order of \(\lambda\): C > D > A > B, i.e. B < A < D < C.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following compounds can exist as cis-trans isomers?
solution: Cis-trans isomerism requires restricted rotation and different groups around the bond. Pent-1-ene (\(\text{CH}_2\)=CH- terminal, identical groups) shows no cis-trans; 2-methylhex-2-ene has two identical methyls on one alkene carbon, no cis-trans; 1,1-dimethylcyclopropane has both methyls on the same carbon, no cis-trans. 1,2-Dimethylcyclohexane can exist as cis and trans isomers.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Phosphoric acid ionizes in three steps with their ionization constant values \(K_{a_1}\), \(K_{a_2}\) and \(K_{a_3}\), respectively, while K is the overall ionization constant. Which of the following statements are true?

A. \(\log K = \log K_{a_1} + \log K_{a_2} + \log K_{a_3}\)
B. \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\) is a stronger acid than \(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^{-}\) and \(\text{HPO}_4^{2-}\)
C. \(K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}\)
D. \(K_{a_1} = \dfrac{K_{a_3} + K_{a_2}}{2}\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: \(\text{H}_3\text{PO}_4\) is a stronger acid than \(\text{H}_2\text{PO}_4^{-}\) and \(\text{HPO}_4^{2-}\) (B true). The stepwise constants are \(K_{a_1} = 7.5\times 10^{-3}\), \(K_{a_2} = 6.2\times 10^{-8}\), \(K_{a_3} = 1.7\times 10^{-12}\), so \(K_{a_1} > K_{a_2} > K_{a_3}\) (C true). The overall constant \(K = K_{a_1}\cdot K_{a_2}\cdot K_{a_3}\), so \(\log K = \log K_{a_1} + \log K_{a_2} + \log K_{a_3}\) (A true). D is false. Correct: A, B and C only.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following reactions does NOT give benzene as the product?
options: \(\text{H-C}\equiv\text{C-H}\) through red hot iron tube at 873 K
solution: Ethyne through a red hot iron tube at 873 K trimerizes to benzene. Sodium benzoate with sodalime undergoes decarboxylation to benzene. n-Hexane over \(\text{Mo}_2\text{O}_3\) undergoes aromatization to benzene. Benzenediazonium chloride with warm water gives phenol (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{OH}\)) + \(\text{N}_2\) + HCl, not benzene. Hence option (4) does not give benzene.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Molar Conductivity and Degree of Dissociation
stem: If the molar conductivity (\(\Lambda_m\)) of a 0.050 mol \(\text{L}^{-1}\) solution of a monobasic weak acid is 90 S \(\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}\), its extent (degree) of dissociation will be [Assume \(\Lambda_+^\circ = 349.6\) S \(\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}\) and \(\Lambda_-^\circ = 50.4\) S \(\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}\).]
solution: Degree of dissociation \(\alpha = \dfrac{\Lambda_m}{\Lambda_m^\circ}\), where \(\Lambda_m^\circ = \Lambda_+^\circ + \Lambda_-^\circ = 349.6 + 50.4 = 400\) S \(\text{cm}^2\ \text{mol}^{-1}\). So \(\alpha = \dfrac{90}{400} = 0.225\).

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: A hypothetical diatomic molecule with bond order zero is quite stable.

Statement II: As bond order increases, the bond length increases.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below:
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: A positive bond order means a stable molecule while a negative or zero bond order means an unstable molecule, so Statement I is false. As bond order increases, the bond length decreases, so Statement II is false. Both statements are false.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Out of the following complex compounds, which of the compound will be having the minimum conductance in solution?
solution: Conductance depends on the number of ions produced (and, for equal numbers, on the charge on the complex unit). \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3]\) and \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_4\text{Cl}_2]\) are non-electrolytes (produce no ions), so they have the minimum conductance. \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]\text{Cl}_3 \rightarrow [\text{Co(NH}_3)_6]^{3+} + 3\text{Cl}^{-}\) (4 ions), \([\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl} \rightarrow [\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{+} + \text{Cl}^{-}\) (2 ions). Official answer: (1) [also marked (2)].

subject: Chemistry
stem: \(\text{C(s)} + 2\text{H}_2\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{CH}_4\text{(g)}\); \(\Delta H = -74.8\) kJ \(\text{mol}^{-1}\). Which of the following diagrams gives an accurate representation of the above reaction? [R \(\rightarrow\) reactants; P \(\rightarrow\) products]
options: Energy profile: reactants (R) at higher level, activation barrier, products (P) at a level 74.8 kJ below R (exothermic, P lower than R)
Energy profile with products (P) above reactants (R) by 74.8 (endothermic-shaped)
Energy profile with a small barrier and P slightly below R (incorrect magnitude/shape)
Energy profile with R and P at similar levels, 74.8 marked (incorrect)
solution: \(\Delta H = -74.8\) kJ \(\text{mol}^{-1}\), so it is an exothermic reaction. The accurate representation has reactants R at a higher energy level, crossing an activation barrier, and products P at a level 74.8 kJ \(\text{mol}^{-1}\) below R. This corresponds to option (1).

subject: Chemistry
stem: The correct order of decreasing basic strength of the given amines is:
solution: Lower the value of \(pK_b\), higher is the basicity; also aliphatic amines are stronger bases than aromatic amines. \(pK_b\): Benzenamine > N-Methylaniline > Ethanamine > N-Ethylethanamine. Hence basic strength: N-Ethylethanamine > Ethanamine > N-Methylaniline > Benzenamine.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Among the following, choose the ones with equal number of atoms.

A. 212 g of \(\text{Na}_2\text{CO}_3\text{(s)}\) [molar mass = 106 g]
B. 248 g of \(\text{Na}_2\text{O(s)}\) [molar mass = 62 g]
C. 240 g of NaOH(s) [molar mass = 40 g]
D. 12 g of \(\text{H}_2\text{(g)}\) [molar mass = 2 g]
E. 220 g of \(\text{CO}_2\text{(g)}\) [molar mass = 44 g]

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Number of atoms = \(\dfrac{\text{given mass}}{\text{molar mass}}\times\text{atomicity}\times N_A\). A: \(\dfrac{212}{106}\times 6\times N_A = 12 N_A\). B: \(\dfrac{248}{62}\times 3\times N_A = 12 N_A\). C: \(\dfrac{240}{40}\times 3\times N_A = 18 N_A\). D: \(\dfrac{12}{2}\times 2\times N_A = 12 N_A\). E: \(\dfrac{220}{44}\times 3\times N_A = 15 N_A\). A, B and D have the same number of atoms (\(12 N_A\)).

| A. Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) | I. Cheilosis |
| B. Vitamin D | II. Convulsions |
| C. Vitamin \(\text{B}_2\) | III. Rickets |
| D. Vitamin \(\text{B}_6\) | IV. Pernicious anaemia |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: Vitamin \(\text{B}_{12}\) deficiency causes Pernicious anaemia (IV). Vitamin D deficiency causes Rickets (III). Vitamin \(\text{B}_2\) deficiency causes Cheilosis (I). Vitamin \(\text{B}_6\) deficiency causes Convulsions (II). Hence A-IV, B-III, C-I, D-II.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The correct order of decreasing acidity of the following aliphatic acids is
solution: Electron donating groups decrease the acidity of carboxylic acids. More alkyl substitution (more electron donation) lowers acidity. So the correct order of decreasing acidity is \(\text{HCOOH} > \text{CH}_3\text{COOH} > (\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CHCOOH} > (\text{CH}_3)_3\text{CCOOH}\).

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: Ferromagnetism is considered as an extreme form of paramagnetism.

Statement II: The number of unpaired electrons in a \(\text{Cr}^{2+}\) ion (Z = 24) is the same as that of a \(\text{Nd}^{3+}\) ion (Z = 60).

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
solution: Substances attracted very strongly in an applied magnetic field are ferromagnetic; ferromagnetism is an extreme form of paramagnetism, so Statement I is correct. \(\text{Cr}^{2+} = 3d^4 4s^0\) has 4 unpaired electrons, while \(\text{Nd}^{3+} = 4f^3 6s^0\) has 3 unpaired electrons. They are not equal, so Statement II is incorrect.

subject: Chemistry
stem: For the reaction \(\text{A(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{B(g)}\), the backward reaction rate constant is higher than the forward reaction rate constant by a factor of 2500, at 1000 K. [Given: R = 0.0831 L atm \(\text{mol}^{-1}\ \text{K}^{-1}\}\)] \(K_P\) for the reaction at 1000 K is
solution: \(K_C = \dfrac{k_f}{k_b} = \dfrac{1}{2500}\). \(K_P = K_C(RT)^{\Delta n_g}\) with \(\Delta n_g = 2 - 1 = 1\). So \(K_P = \dfrac{1}{2500}\times 0.0831\times 1000 = 0.033\).

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements:

Statement-I: Benzenediazonium salt is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K. It decomposes easily in the dry state.

Statement-II: Insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult and hence iodobenzene is prepared through the reaction of benzenediazonium salt with KI.

In the light of the above statements, choose the most appropriate answer from the options given below :
options: Both Statement I and Statement II are correct
Both Statement I and Statement II are incorrect
Statement I is correct but Statement II is incorrect
Statement I is incorrect but Statement II is correct
solution: Benzene diazonium chloride is prepared by the reaction of aniline with nitrous acid at 273-278 K: \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{NH}_2 + \text{NaNO}_2 + 2\text{HCl} \rightarrow \text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{N}_2^{+}\text{Cl}^{-} + \text{NaCl} + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}\), and it decomposes easily in the dry state (Statement I correct). Iodobenzene is prepared by shaking benzene diazonium salt with KI because direct insertion of iodine into the benzene ring is difficult (Statement II correct). Both statements are correct.

subject: Chemistry
stem: How many products (including stereoisomers) are expected from monochlorination of the following compound? (2-methylbutane / isopentane, \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\))
solution: Possible monochlorination products: (i) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{Cl}\), one isomer; (ii) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CH-CHCl-CH}_3\), two isomers due to the chiral carbon; (iii) \((\text{CH}_3)_2\text{CCl-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\), one isomer; (iv) \(\text{ClCH}_2(\text{CH}_3)\text{CH-CH}_2\text{-CH}_3\), two isomers due to the chiral carbon. Total 6 isomers.

subject: Chemistry
stem: Among the given compounds I-III, the correct order of bond dissociation energy of the C-H bond marked with * is: (I = benzene with * on ring C-H; II = phenylacetylene with * on the terminal alkyne C-H; III = methylenecyclopropane / a cyclopropane-based compound with * on an sp3 C-H)
solution: I: the * carbon is \(sp^2\) hybridised. II: the * carbon is \(sp\) hybridised. III: the * carbon is \(sp^3\) hybridised. Higher the percentage s-character, stronger is the C-H bond. Correct order of bond dissociation energy of the C-H bond: II (\(sp\)) > I (\(sp^2\)) > III (\(sp^3\)).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which one of the following compounds does not decolourize bromine water? (Options: cyclohexane; phenol; styrene / phenyl-CH=CH2; aniline)
solution: The reddish orange colour of bromine solution discharges when bromine adds to an unsaturated site. Styrene adds \(\text{Br}_2\) (colour discharge). Aniline and phenol undergo electrophilic bromination to form tribromo derivatives (colour discharge). Cyclohexane (a saturated compound) does not react with \(\text{Br}_2\) in \(\text{CCl}_4\); no discharge of orange colour. Hence cyclohexane does not decolourize bromine water.

subject: Chemistry
stem: The major product of the following reaction is: a substrate bearing a phenyl ketone (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CN}\)) treated with (i) \(\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}\) (excess); (ii) \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}\).
options: A tertiary alcohol at the ketone carbon while the nitrile is retained (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-C(CH}_3)(\text{OH})\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CN}\))
A tertiary alcohol at the former ketone carbon and a methyl ketone from the nitrile (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-C(CH}_3)(\text{OH})\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CO-CH}_3\))
Two hydroxyl groups (double addition giving a diol-type product with two \(\text{CH}_3\) at the far end)
A phenyl ketone retained with a methyl ketone from the nitrile (both C=O retained)
solution: Excess \(\text{CH}_3\text{MgBr}\) adds to the ketone to give, after \(\text{H}_3\text{O}^{+}\), a tertiary alcohol (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-C(CH}_3)(\text{OH})-\)), and adds once to the nitrile to give (after hydrolysis of the imine) a methyl ketone (\(\text{-CO-CH}_3\)). The major product is \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-C(OH)(CH}_3)\text{-CH}_2\text{-CH}_2\text{-CO-CH}_3\).

subject: Chemistry
stem: Which of the following aqueous solution will exhibit highest boiling point?
solution: \(\Delta T_b = i K_b\times m\), so \(\Delta T_b \propto i\times m\). Taking molarity \(\approx\) molality: Urea \(i\times m = 1\times 0.01 = 0.01\); \(\text{KNO}_3 = 2\times 0.01 = 0.02\); \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4 = 3\times 0.01 = 0.03\); \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_{12}\text{O}_6 = 1\times 0.015 = 0.015\). Higher the value of \(i\times m\), higher the boiling point. \(\text{Na}_2\text{SO}_4\) has the highest value, hence the highest boiling point.

| A. Haber process | I. Fe catalyst |
| B. Wacker oxidation | II. \(\text{PdCl}_2\) |

| D. Ziegler catalyst | IV. \(\text{TiCl}_4\) with \(\text{Al(CH}_3)_3\) |

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Haber process uses Fe catalyst (I). Wacker oxidation uses \(\text{PdCl}_2\) (II). Wilkinson catalyst is \([(\text{PPh}_3)_3\text{RhCl}]\) (III). Ziegler catalyst is \(\text{TiCl}_4\) with \(\text{Al(CH}_3)_3\) (IV). Hence A-I, B-II, C-III, D-IV.

subject: Chemistry
stem: 5 moles of liquid X and 10 moles of liquid Y make a solution having a vapour pressure of 70 torr. The vapour pressures of pure X and Y are 63 torr and 78 torr respectively. Which of the following is true regarding the described solution?
options: The solution has volume greater than the sum of individual volumes.
solution: \(P_{total} = X_x P_x^\circ + X_y P_y^\circ = \dfrac{5}{15}\times 63 + \dfrac{10}{15}\times 78 = 21 + 52 = 73\) torr. The observed total pressure is 70 torr, which is less than the calculated 73 torr, hence the solution shows negative deviation.

stem: Identify the suitable reagent for the following conversion: methyl benzoate (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-OCH}_3\)) is converted to benzaldehyde (\(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CHO}\)).
solution: Esters are reduced to aldehydes with DIBAL-H (\(\text{AlH(iBu)}_2\)). \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CO-OCH}_3\) with (i) DIBAL-H then (ii) \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) gives benzaldehyde \(\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{-CHO}\).

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Given below are two statements: one is labelled as Assertion (A) and the other is labelled as Reason (R).

Assertion (A): An alkyl iodide undergoes \(S_N2\) reaction faster than the corresponding alkyl chloride.

Reason (R): Iodine is a better leaving group because of its large size.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:
options: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
Both A and R are true but R is not the correct explanation of A
A is true but R is false
A is false but R is true
solution: The rate of \(S_N2\) reaction of the alkyl iodide is faster than that of the alkyl chloride because iodine is a good leaving group due to its large size, which stabilises the \(\text{I}^{-}\) ion. Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A.

subtopic: Hess's Law and Heat of Formation
stem: The standard heat of formation, in kcal/mol of \(\text{Ba}^{2+}\) is : [Given: standard heat of formation of \(\text{SO}_4^{2-}\) ion (aq) = \(-216\) kcal/mol, standard heat of crystallisation of \(\text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)} = -4.5\) kcal/mol, standard heat of formation of \(\text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)} = -349\) kcal/mol]
solution: Given: (1) \(\text{S} + 2\text{O}_2 + 2e^{-} \rightarrow \text{SO}_4^{2-}\), \(\Delta H_f = -216\); (2) \(\text{Ba}^{2+}\text{(g)} + \text{SO}_4^{2-}\text{(g)} \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)}\), \(\Delta H_{cryst} = -4.5\); (3) \(\text{Ba} + \text{S} + 2\text{O}_2 \rightarrow \text{BaSO}_4\text{(s)}\), \(\Delta H_{f(\text{BaSO}_4)} = -349\). The target (4) is \(\text{Ba(s)} \rightarrow \text{Ba}^{2+}\text{(g)} + 2e^{-}\). Applying (3) \(-\) (1) \(-\) (2): \(-349 - (-4.5) - (-216) = -349 + 4.5 + 216 = -128.5\) kcal/mol.

stem: Total number of possible isomers (both structural as well as stereoisomers) of cyclic ethers of molecular formula \(\text{C}_4\text{H}_8\text{O}\) is :
solution: For cyclic ethers the O must be in the ring. Counting each structural isomer with its stereoisomers (where a chiral centre is present): 2-methyloxetane 2(d,l pair); oxetane substituted 1; tetrahydrofuran 1; 2-methylepoxide (isomer) 1; 2,3-dimethyloxirane meso 1 + (d,l) 2; ethyloxirane 2(d,l pair); etc. Total number of isomers = 2 + 1 + 1 + 1 + 2 + 1 + 2 = 10.

subject: Chemistry
subtopic: Molecular Properties - Dipole, Lone Pairs, Bond Length, Bond Enthalpy
stem:
Identify the correct orders against the property mentioned

A. \(\text{H}_2\text{O} > \text{NH}_3 > \text{CHCl}_3\) - dipole moment
B. \(\text{XeF}_4 > \text{XeO}_3 > \text{XeF}_2\) - number of lone pairs on central atom
C. O-H > C-H > N-O - bond length
D. \(\text{N}_2 > \text{O}_2 > \text{H}_2\) - bond enthalpy

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
solution: A: dipole moments \(\text{H}_2\text{O}\) 1.85 D > \(\text{NH}_3\) 1.47 D > \(\text{CHCl}_3\) 1.04 D — correct. B: lone pairs — \(\text{XeF}_4\) has 2, \(\text{XeO}_3\) has 1, \(\text{XeF}_2\) has 3, so the order is wrong. C: correct bond length order is N-O > C-H > O-H, so the given order is wrong. D: bond order/enthalpy \(\text{N}_2\) (bond order 3) > \(\text{O}_2\) (bond order 2) > \(\text{H}_2\) (bond order 1) — correct. Correct: A, D only.

subject: Chemistry
stem:
Higher yield of NO in \(\text{N}_2\text{(g)} + \text{O}_2\text{(g)} \rightleftharpoons 2\text{NO(g)}\) can be obtained at [\(\Delta H\) of the reaction = +180.7 kJ \(\text{mol}^{-1}\)]

A. Higher temperature
B. Lower temperature
C. Higher concentration of \(\text{N}_2\)
D. Higher concentration of \(\text{O}_2\)

Choose the correct answer from the options given below :
solution: Yield depends on temperature, concentration of reactants/products, and pressure. Since the reaction is endothermic (\(\Delta H = +180.7\) kJ \(\text{mol}^{-1}\)), increasing temperature shifts the equilibrium forward, increasing NO yield. Increasing the concentration of reactants \(\text{N}_2\) and \(\text{O}_2\) also shifts the equilibrium forward. Hence A, C and D only increase the yield of NO.

chapter: Organic Chemistry – Some Basic Principles and Techniques
stem: Which one of the following reactions does NOT belong to "Lassaigne's test"?
solution: Nitrogen, sulphur, halogens and phosphorus present in an organic compound are detected by Lassaigne's test, which involves fusion with sodium: \(\text{Na} + \text{C} + \text{N} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaCN}\), \(2\text{Na} + \text{S} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{Na}_2\text{S}\), \(\text{Na} + \text{X} \xrightarrow{\Delta} \text{NaX}\) (X = Cl, Br, I). The reaction \(2\text{CuO} + \text{C} \xrightarrow{\Delta} 2\text{Cu} + \text{CO}_2\) does not belong to Lassaigne's test.
